sourceNote: Rule texts were read from the canonical Obsidian developer documentation sources listed in `sources`. docs.obsidian.md is an Obsidian Publish site whose HTML shell does not expose page content to plain HTTP fetchers; the same pages are published from obsidianmd/obsidian-developer-docs and were read from there. Both locations are recorded per rule. Re-verify before relying on this map: Obsidian may change these policies at any time.

typescript-api.note: The published API surface was verified against the obsidian typings shipped with the pinned devDependency rather than the rendered docs site.

categories.MUST: Mandatory to stay listed in the Obsidian Community directory, or mandatory to be published.
categories.SHOULD: Documented recommendation. Obsidian states it may still require these to be addressed depending on severity.
categories.INFORMATIONAL: Context that shapes the audit but is not itself a pass/fail rule.

rules.name: No obfuscated code
rules.description: Plugins and themes must not obfuscate code to hide its purpose.
rules.verification: Automated heuristics over src/ and the built bundle: eval/Function constructors, packed/hex-encoded blobs, single-line source files, base64 payloads above a size threshold. Minification of the release bundle is explicitly not obfuscation.

rules.name: No dynamic ads loaded over the internet
rules.description: Plugins and themes must not insert dynamic ads that are loaded over the internet.
rules.verification: The full network endpoint inventory is enumerated from source; any endpoint that is not a declared model provider or the user-configured Local API is a finding.

rules.name: No static ads outside the plugin's own interface
rules.description: Plugins must not insert static ads outside a plugin's own interface.
rules.verification: No automated signal is reliable here. Reviewed by reading the UI construction code.

rules.name: No client-side telemetry
rules.description: Plugins and themes must not include client-side telemetry.
rules.verification: Scans source and the built bundle for known analytics SDK names and hostnames (Sentry, PostHog, Google Analytics, Mixpanel, Amplitude, Segment, Datadog, New Relic, Bugsnag, Rollbar, …) and for any outbound request target that is not on the allowlist in .compliance/ai-vault-policy.json. Also flags transmission of device, install, user or vault identifiers.

rules.name: No self-installation or self-update
rules.description: Plugins and themes must not install or update themselves or their dependencies.
rules.verification: Scans for runtime code download/execution: child_process, dynamic import of remote URLs, writes into the plugin directory, eval of fetched content.

rules.name: Disclose that payment is required for full access
rules.description: Payment required for full access is only allowed if clearly indicated in the README.
rules.verification: The plugin itself charges nothing; the model providers do. Checked by asserting the README states that an OpenAI/Anthropic account and paid API usage may be required.

rules.name: Disclose that an account is required for full access
rules.description: An account required for full access is only allowed if clearly indicated in the README.
rules.verification: Asserts the README names the third-party accounts and API keys the plugin needs.

rules.name: Disclose network use and name the remote services
rules.description: Network use is only allowed if clearly indicated in the README, clearly explaining which remote services are used and why they're needed.
rules.verification: Cross-check: every network host reachable from source must be named in README.md and PRIVACY.md, and every host named in the docs must exist in the code. A mismatch in either direction fails.

rules.name: Disclose access to files outside Obsidian vaults
rules.description: Accessing files outside of Obsidian vaults is only allowed if clearly indicated in the README, clearly explaining why this is needed.
rules.verification: This plugin writes history, projects, the RAG index and keys.json to a directory next to the vault. The check asserts that README.md and PRIVACY.md state that files outside the vault are written, name the default location, and explain the reason.

rules.name: Disclose static ads inside the plugin's own interface
rules.description: Static ads such as banners and pop-up messages within the plugin's own interface are only allowed if clearly indicated in the README.
rules.verification: Not applicable unless ads are added; confirmed by reading the UI code.

rules.name: Disclose server-side telemetry and link a privacy policy
rules.description: Server-side telemetry is only allowed if clearly indicated in the README, and a link to a privacy policy that explains how the data is handled must be included.
rules.verification: The plugin operates no server of its own. The check asserts there is no first-party backend endpoint in the code and that PRIVACY.md states this explicitly.

rules.name: Disclose closed-source code
rules.description: Closed-source code is only allowed if clearly indicated in the README; handled case by case.
rules.verification: Asserts the repository ships the full TypeScript source for everything bundled into main.js and that no pre-built binary blob is committed.

rules.name: Include a LICENSE file and indicate the license
rules.description: All community plugins must include a LICENSE file and clearly indicate the license of the plugin.
rules.verification: Asserts LICENSE exists, package.json declares a license, and the README names it.

rules.name: Comply with the licenses of code you use
rules.description: Comply with the original licenses of any code the plugin makes use of, including attribution in the README if required.
rules.verification: License inventory of the dependency tree against the allow/deny lists in .compliance/ai-vault-policy.json. Attribution obligations for copyleft licences require a human decision.

rules.name: Respect the Obsidian trademark
rules.description: Don't use the "Obsidian" trademark in a way that could confuse users into thinking the plugin is a first-party creation.
rules.verification: Checks that manifest.json `name` and `id` do not begin with "Obsidian" and that the description does not claim first-party status. Final judgement is human.

rules.name: Forks require permission or a documented unreachable author
rules.description: Forks are not allowed in the Community directory unless they have explicit written approval from the original author, or proof that the author is unreachable under the stated timeline.
rules.verification: Cannot be established from the repository contents alone.

rules.name: Only use fundingUrl for financial support links
rules.description: Use fundingUrl if you accept financial support. If you don't accept donations, remove fundingUrl from your manifest.
rules.verification: Asserts fundingUrl is either absent or a valid https URL.

rules.name: Set an appropriate minAppVersion
rules.description: minAppVersion should be the minimum required version of the Obsidian app the plugin is compatible with.
rules.verification: Asserts minAppVersion is present and semver-shaped, and that versions.json maps the current version to it. Whether the declared floor is actually correct for the APIs used requires a human check against the API surface.

rules.name: Keep the plugin description short and simple
rules.description: 250 characters maximum, ends with a period, avoids emoji and special characters, does not start with "This is a plugin", and uses correct capitalization for proper nouns.
rules.verification: String checks over manifest.json `description`.

rules.name: Set isDesktopOnly when using Node.js or Electron APIs
rules.description: If your plugin uses Node.js or Electron APIs you must set isDesktopOnly to true in the manifest.
rules.verification: If any source file imports a Node built-in or electron, manifest.isDesktopOnly must be true.

rules.name: Don't include the plugin ID in command IDs
rules.description: Obsidian automatically prefixes command IDs with the plugin ID.
rules.verification: Extracts addCommand id literals and asserts none starts with the manifest id.

rules.name: Remove all sample plugin code
rules.description: Sample code from the sample plugin must be removed before submission.
rules.verification: Searches for sample-plugin identifiers (MyPlugin, MyPluginSettings, SampleSettingTab, SampleModal, 'Sample Plugin').

rules.name: Avoid the global app instance
rules.description: Use this.app rather than the global app or window.app.
rules.verification: Searches for window.app and bare global app usage.

rules.name: Avoid unnecessary console logging
rules.description: In its default configuration the developer console should only show error messages; debug messages should not be shown.
rules.verification: Counts console.* calls and, more importantly for this audit, asserts that no logging call passes note content, prompts, conversation history, RAG chunks or an API key.

rules.name: Avoid innerHTML, outerHTML and insertAdjacentHTML
rules.description: Building DOM elements from user-defined input with innerHTML, outerHTML or insertAdjacentHTML can pose a security risk.
rules.verification: Static scan of src/ for the three sinks plus document.write and Element.setHTMLUnsafe.

rules.name: Clean up resources when the plugin unloads
rules.description: Resources such as event listeners must be destroyed or released on unload; prefer registerEvent() and registerDomEvent().
rules.verification: Flags addEventListener calls on long-lived targets (document, window) that are not paired with a removal, and confirms vault/workspace subscriptions go through registerEvent.

rules.name: Prefer the Vault API over the Adapter API
rules.description: The Vault API has a caching layer and performs file operations serially, avoiding race conditions.
rules.verification: Counts vault.adapter usages and reports where they occur, so each can be justified or replaced.

rules.name: Use normalizePath() for user-defined paths
rules.description: normalizePath() scrubs a path to be safe for the file system and for cross-platform use.
rules.verification: Reports vault-relative paths built from user input that do not pass through normalizePath. Paths outside the vault are handled by the containment helpers in src/security/paths.ts instead, which normalizePath does not cover.

rules.name: No hardcoded styling
rules.description: Use CSS classes with Obsidian's CSS variables instead of assigning styles from JavaScript.
rules.verification: Covered by eslint-plugin-obsidianmd during npm run lint.

rules.name: Don't commit main.js to the repository
rules.description: Only include main.js in releases, not in the repository.
rules.verification: Asserts main.js is git-ignored and not tracked.

rules.name: Use requestUrl instead of fetch
rules.description: Don't use fetch or axios; use Obsidian's requestUrl.
rules.verification: Asserts no fetch/XMLHttpRequest/WebSocket/sendBeacon call exists in src/, and that every outbound call goes through requestUrl.

rules.name: Commit and use a lock file
rules.description: Commit and use a lock file when using a package manager.
rules.verification: Asserts package-lock.json is tracked, is in sync with package.json, pins resolved URLs to the public npm registry and records integrity hashes.

rules.name: Use trashFile instead of deleting vault files directly
rules.description: Don't use vault.delete to delete files; use FileManager.trashFile so the file is removed according to the user's preferences.
rules.verification: Flags vault.delete / adapter.remove calls that target vault files.

rules.name: Gate FileSystemAdapter behind an instanceof check
rules.description: Don't cast Vault.adapter to FileSystemAdapter; gate all usage behind instanceof.
rules.verification: Asserts every FileSystemAdapter reference is inside an instanceof guard.

rules.name: Avoid `as any`
rules.description: Don't use `as any`; use proper typing instead.
rules.verification: Static scan for `as any` and `: any` in src/.

rules.name: Don't hardcode the .obsidian configuration folder
rules.description: The configuration directory can be customized; use Vault.configDir.
rules.verification: Searches for a literal ".obsidian" path in src/.

rules.name: Disclose the required information in the README
rules.description: Disclose payments, account requirements, network use, external file access, ads, telemetry with privacy policy, and closed-source code in the README.
rules.verification: Aggregate of OBS-POL-006 through OBS-POL-012 plus the required-sections check over README.md and PRIVACY.md.

rules.name: Publish main.js, manifest.json and styles.css as release assets
rules.description: The release must contain the built plugin assets. styles.css may be omitted only if the plugin ships none.
rules.verification: Asserts the release workflow uploads all three files, and that a clean build produces main.js.

rules.name: Generate a build provenance attestation for release assets
rules.description: A signed build provenance attestation for the release assets is recommended when submitting a plugin to the community directory.
rules.verification: Asserts the release workflow runs an attestation action and that its subject-path covers every published asset.

rules.name: The release tag must match the manifest version
rules.description: Create a tag that matches the version in manifest.json; the tag must be plain semver.
rules.verification: Asserts manifest.json, package.json, package-lock.json and versions.json agree, and that a matching git tag exists.

rules.name: Plugins inherit the application's full access
rules.description: Obsidian states it cannot reliably restrict plugins to specific permissions; plugins can access files, connect to the internet and install additional programs. Users are advised to audit plugins that handle sensitive data.
rules.verification: Context for the audit: there is no sandbox to rely on, so every capability the plugin takes must be justified and disclosed.

rules.name: SecretStorage is the documented place for API keys
rules.description: SecretStorage provides a central key-value store for secrets. Settings should hold the NAME of a secret, not the secret value, and SecretComponent should replace a plain text input.
rules.verification: Reports whether the plugin uses app.secretStorage/SecretComponent. Adopting it raises the required minAppVersion, so the decision is explicitly a product decision, not an automated fix.
rules.notes: SecretStorage and SecretComponent were exposed to plugins in the Obsidian 1.11.x line (see https://obsidian.md/changelog/2026-01-07-desktop-v1.11.4/). The plugin currently declares minAppVersion 1.7.2, so adopting the API means dropping support for every 1.7–1.10 install.
